A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ZeroDiff, despite the changed title and format. Their methods, experiments, figures, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ZSL/GZSL experiments on AWA2, CUB, and SUN, including component ablations, reduced-data evaluations, sensitivity studies, and discriminator analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional component/input ablations, critic-score diagnostics, and representation analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The DFG/DRG generators, CE/SC extractors, three discriminators, mutual-learning objective, and training/testing Algorithms 1–3 remain substantively unchanged. Dynamic instance-level semantics is a revised interpretation of the existing SC representation input.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K pretraining and evaluate ZSL/GZSL on AWA2, CUB, and SUN, including 30% and 10% training subsets. The new class-prototype and fox visualizations analyze retained datasets without introducing another task or population.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds ICIS, ZSLViT, DSP, DML, VADS, CLIP, CoOp, and CoOp+SHIP, while removing several earlier comparators, including APN, I2DFormer, MSDN, TransZero++, IAB, APN+TFVAEGAN, and CMC-GAN. The limited-data comparison adds f-CLSWGAN and removes SDVAE. The evaluated DDGAN comparison also disappears.

E3.justification: The principal dataset splits, accuracy metrics, and reduced-data sampling protocol remain unchanged. Additional analyses introduce discriminator/input controls and an eight-class CUB prototype comparison; the gamma sweep extends from 0–2 to 0–2.5. Mutual-learning diagnostics switch from comparing three datasets to comparing three training-data fractions on AWA2.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands component controls in Table 3 and adds DFG input ablations in Table 4. New analyses examine baseline critic gaps under data scarcity, prototype similarities, SC representation geometry, and mutual-loss sensitivity. Conversely, the DDGAN denoising-step study is removed, and the mutual-learning diagnostic experiment is replaced.

E5.justification: v1 specifies fixed seeds 9182, 3483, and 4115 for AWA2, CUB, and SUN; v2 omits this information. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty estimates or confidence intervals. The shading in v2 Figure 9 represents performance improvements, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Reported ZeroDiff AWA2 T1/H changes from 86.4/79.5 to 87.3/81.4, while headline CUB/SUN scores remain unchanged. Reduced-data f-VAEGAN results also change, including AWA2 at 10% from 65.1/40.0 to 73.1/54.4; ZeroDiff's reduced-data entries are retained. Added and removed comparison, ablation, and diagnostic results substantially revise the evidence. The PDFs do not explain the headline score revisions.

T1.justification: The substantive diffusion equations, loss definitions, and mathematical reasoning remain equivalent. In particular, v2's emphasized critic-gap definitions already appear as Equations 18–19 in v1 and become Equations 4 and 16. No substantive new theoretical assumptions, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: v2 makes identifying and quantifying spurious visual-semantic correlation a central contribution and attributes scarce-data degradation largely to that problem. This replaces v1's emphasis on class/instance efficiency and its explicit first-diffusion-ZSL and first-discriminator-mutual-learning novelty claims. The broad performance and data-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 motivates SC representations through missing potential semantics; v2 emphasizes mismatches between static class labels and individual instances, interpreting intra-class variation as dynamic semantics. It adds interpretations of VADS's discriminability tradeoff and diffusion-time conditioning. Earlier conclusions about semantic rectification under scarce data and one-step generation relative to DDGAN are removed.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised code release with a stated repository and adds selected mutual-loss and smoothing settings. However, v1 Table A1's dataset-specific synthesis counts, learning rates, and batch sizes for ZeroDiff and baselines disappear, as does the data-access statement. Much of the remaining implementation information is relocated to Appendix A.2.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned around visual-semantic correlation, dynamic semantic prototypes, and data-efficient generation. v2 adds discussion of DSP, VADS, causal visual-semantic work, DiffAugment, AdvAug, and PatchDiff, replacing much of the generic diffusion overview. It also drops the earlier explicit first-of-its-kind assertions.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, related work, and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten. The method is reorganized around three motivating insights; implementation details and the CE-versus-SC discussion move into an expanded appendix, and references precede the appendices. These changes substantially alter the document's narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly two-column formatting to a single-column conference layout. Separate ZSL/GZSL tables are merged with backbone and feature-setting columns, Figure 1 is redrawn, and new diagnostic plots, heatmaps, and representation visualizations are added. Existing analyses are also replotted or relocated, including the CE/SC comparison and generated-feature t-SNE.

improvement.justification: Expanded component/input controls and new critic-gap and representation diagnostics provide better support for the method's design and scarce-data argument. The net gain is limited by removal of detailed hyperparameters, seeds, the DDGAN study, and SDVAE's strong limited-data results. Numerical discussion also remains inconsistent: v2 Section 4.3 reports AWA2 H as 79.5 despite Table 1 showing 81.4. These omissions and inconsistencies constrain the benefit of the stronger analyses.
